summary: Climate network stability analysis for H002: global mean albedo 2000-2012 = 0.2996, 2013-2025 = 0.2965, change = -0.0031 (p=0.003) — statistically significant but small (~1% relative decrease). Both values remain near the ~29% range H002 predicts physical constants constrain. Network centrality ranks are moderately stable (Spearman r=0.554, p<10^-40) — the same regions remain network hubs across both periods. Cell-level CV = 0.144 (14% relative variability) while global mean CV ≈ 3% — the global mean is ~5x more stable than local values, consistent with spatial averaging and compensating regional changes preserving the global mean. INTERPRETATION: H002 partially supported — the ~29% global mean is maintained (invariant constraint active) but shows a small declining trend, suggesting the constraint is not perfectly rigid. The secular decline (~1% over 25 years) may reflect the changing conditions (Arctic sea ice loss, cloud changes) that are central to the Feldman 2026 paper.
